response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT p.SEX, AVG(l.CPK * 1.0 / NULLIF(l.GPT, 0)) AS a FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.SEX), s1 AS (SELECT SEX, a, (SELECT AVG(a) FROM r) AS m1 FROM r), k1 AS (SELECT * FROM s1 WHERE a > m1), k2 AS (SELECT *, (SELECT AVG(a) FROM k1) AS m2 FROM k1), k3 AS (SELECT * FROM k2 WHERE a > m2) SELECT AVG(a) AS avg_ratio, AVG(a - m1) AS avg_above_first_mean, AVG(a - m2) AS avg_above_second_mean FROM k3

assumptions.assumption: The ratio is CPK/GPT per lab row. It is missing when CPK or GPT is NULL, or when GPT is 0 (NULLIF turns the division into NULL). Such rows are ignored.
Patients with NULL SEX are not treated as a sex value and are excluded.

The first mean is the unweighted mean of the per-sex averages. The second mean is the mean of the averages of the sexes that survived the first filter, and 'above' is strict. If only one sex survives the first filter, its average equals the second mean, so no rows remain and the result is NULL.
